narration.text: AI is fighting fire with fire. Today, Reddit is using AI to solve a problem AI largely created. We will explain how. Also, new apps protect against AI scams, and the UK financial regulator issues a stark warning. Let's dive in.
TechCrunch reports that Reddit is using large language models to tackle spam. In the AI era, platforms must fight fire with fire to cull unwanted content. It is a necessary move for online safety.
Savi's new app aims to protect consumers from realistic AI scams. TechCrunch says the company just raised seven million dollars in funding. The app launches for iPhone and Android this week.
Ars Technica reports that the UK regulator warns of an 'arms race' in financial services. An official makes a case for greater watchdog powers. Millions now use AI for personal finance decisions.
Ars Technica also explains how AI could enable autonomous robot workers. Top robotics researchers detail how robot autonomy is evolving. This could transform workplaces and even homes.
That's your AI news for today. Which story do you think is most impactful? Let us know in the comments below. Follow for tomorrow's AI brief.

description: Daily AI news for a general audience. Today, Reddit uses AI to combat spam. A new app from Savi protects against AI scams. The UK financial regulator warns of an 'arms race' as AI use grows. Also, autonomous robots could soon be common in workplaces.
